::: {.research-intro}
I build nanopores and measure the electrical signals that molecules produce as they pass through them. At the [BAST Laboratory](https://bastlabs.org/) at Southern Methodist University, I study how pore geometry and material interfaces change those signals and develop instruments that make nanopore experiments easier to run.

[Publications](publications.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Research techniques and skills](experience.qmd#research-techniques-and-skills){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

## Current research

:::: {.research-grid .research-grid-current}

::: {.research-card}
### α-Hemolysin hybrid nanopores {#alpha-hemolysin}

[2026–present]{.research-period}

I lead work on combining α-hemolysin, a biological pore, with a quartz nanopipette. I use electrical measurements to characterize the resulting hybrid device and study its stability for single-molecule sensing.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### P.O.R.E. nanopore fabrication {#pore}

[2026–present]{.research-period}

I co-developed a programmable instrument that fabricates solid-state nanopores using controlled dielectric breakdown. I led the mechanical and fluidic design, built interchangeable flow-cell cartridges, and helped validate the assembled system.

[Read about the instrument](projects/instrumentation.qmd)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Modeling and machine learning {#modeling}

[Cross-project research]{.research-period}

I use electric-field simulations to relate pore structure to molecular transport. I also analyze current blockade and dwell-time measurements to see how pore architecture and transport direction affect the recorded signals.

[Explore modeling and signal analysis](projects/modeling-ml.qmd)
:::

::::

## Published projects

:::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}
### Multilayer nanopores

[2025–2026]{.research-period}

I co-led experiments on silicon nitride membranes layered with graphene, molybdenum disulfide, or hexagonal boron nitride. We found that the choice and arrangement of layers changed the electrical signatures of protein transport, including how those signatures varied with direction.

[Explore multilayer nanopores](projects/heterostructures.qmd)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Collaborative molecular sensing

[2024–2026]{.research-period}

I contributed nanopore measurements and data analysis to studies of [dendrimer–peptide conjugates](https://doi.org/10.1002/admi.70569), [ferritin subunits](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c00914), and [short peptides](https://doi.org/10.1002/elps.8122).
:::

::: {.research-card}
### DNA-templated silver nanoclusters

[2024–2025]{.research-period}

I co-led electrical and fluorescence measurements to examine how applied voltage and electrolyte composition affect DNA-templated silver nanoclusters. Under conditions that stabilized the clusters, nanopore measurements distinguished cluster-bearing DNA from the DNA templates alone.

[Explore silver nanocluster sensing](projects/silver-nanoclusters.qmd)
:::

::: {.research-card}
### DNA origami hybrid nanopores

[2023–2024]{.research-period}

I led experiments placing three-dimensional DNA origami inside silicon nitride nanopores and tested how the hybrid structure affected protein transport measurements. The hybrid pore improved sensitivity for human serum transferrin compared with the solid-state pore alone.

[Explore the DNA origami project](projects/dna-origami.qmd)
:::

::::

## Earlier engineering research

At SEGi University, I used computational fluid dynamics to compare forward- and backward-swept C-wing configurations at supersonic speeds. The project received an IMechE Project Award. I also co-authored a [review of 3D printing in orthopedic surgery](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0165255).
